elements.id-string-3: We show that a randomly perturbed digraph, where we start with a dense digraph $D_\alpha$ and add a small number of random edges to it, will typically contain a fixed orientation of a bounded-degree spanning tree.This answers a question posed by Araujo, Balogh, Krueger, Piga and Treglown and generalizes the corresponding result for randomly perturbed graphs by Krivelevich, Kwan and Sudakov.More specifically, we prove that there exists a constant $c = c(\alpha, \Delta)$ such that if $T$ is an oriented tree with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $D_\alpha$ is an $n$-vertex digraph  with minimum semidegree $\alpha n$, then the graph obtained by adding $cn$ uniformly random edges to $D_\alpha$ will contain $T$ with high probability.
